requirements.text: clamp(x, lo, hi) returns lo when x < lo, hi when x > hi, and x otherwise (for lo <= hi).
requirements.reason: The claim requires clamp to return x for every input, even when the bounds are ordered and x lies outside them. For example, clamp(7, 2, 5) is required to return 5, but the claim specifies 7.

claims.summary: For every choice of three 32-bit inputs, the export named “clamp” returns its first input unchanged.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Mislabeled.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi] [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x]
claims.name: Examples.Mislabeled.clamp
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `x` clamped into the range `[lo, hi]`.
details: Covers every 32-bit pattern for the three inputs: the first value and two bounds.
The values are passed as 32-bit Wasm integers; the claim does not interpret them as signed or unsigned arithmetic values.
The result must be the first input unchanged, with no arithmetic or wraparound specified.
Returns additionally guarantees that the module can be instantiated and that every call in every fresh instance and host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly that value.
caveats: Despite the export name, this does not specify clamp behavior: it requires the result to equal the first input, regardless of the bounds.
It does not constrain memory effects or other internal behavior.
